cb8177b26c0bdd1f.text: Blanche's answer on the record neither confirms nor denies that any investigation of Huang was opened. The two anonymous accounts go further: by them, Huang was never a target or subject, so there was no case against him to clear him of.

findings.problem: "Huang was never a target or subject" turns the officials' account of what Blanche said on November 21 into a claim about all time; the only "never" in the records is the Examiner source's, and that covers just the Megaspeed case.

adf2e06c49f02eeb.text: Five inquiries remain open, each into something different.

findings.problem: Counting the SEC examination among five inquiries that "remain open" states as fact what two unnamed people told Reuters.
The claim says only that the Justice Department took the lead in a criminal investigation of Megaspeed; the block tells readers that investigation is still open now.

30a49da832136053.text: Huang's House interviews were set before his return, after the committee released Commerce's China chip-license table. Democrats preparing to investigate Nvidia have widened the inquiry to Trump's role in bringing Huang back, The Washington Post reports. The hearings can ask Curtis's question, who gave the board its assurance; they do not close the Justice Department's Megaspeed case or the SEC, California and Missouri inquiries.

findings.problem: The block says the House interviews were set after the committee released Commerce's China chip-license table, which none of its claims holds.
No claim says Huang's interviews were scheduled before his return or after the committee released Commerce's China chip-license table.

0a6e2f4ac61ab4bb.text: The board says it relied on the government's input; why that input was given is Schumer's charge to make, and his to prove.

findings.problem: A reader would think Schumer made a specific charge about why the government gave the board its input, but the claim only has him saying Trump is putting his own and his billionaire friends' financial interests before national security, and that Democrats will investigate.
